segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman, and thank you,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Mr. Donahoe. It is good to see you again. Good to see

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: you. I have a few questions. When was the last year the Postal Service had a profit?
I

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_05
segments.text: think we had a profit in 2006, maybe 2007. I can't be 100 percent sure of one of those two years.
Okay, thanks.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_08
segments.text: How much money did the Postal

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: Service lose in the first quarter of 2012? With our requirement to pre-fund about $3 billion and $300 million. And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_10
segments.text: how much do you expect to lose for the entire fiscal year? Depending on

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: how we finish the year, probably in the vicinity of about $14 billion. We are a little ahead of our revenue.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: revenues right now and people have done a great job holding costs. The pre-funding for this year counts for both this year and last, so that is $11 billion of those. Last

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_16
segments.text: year,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Congress acted at the last second to give you some temporary relief from the pre-funding.
What

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: does the lack of certainty of whether or not you will have to make your payment each year do for your plan for profitability and your overall business model?
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: have to get that resolved. That is what we are proposing right now in terms of the health care proposals and the overall plan. But I will tell you, it is much larger than us. This is an industry issue.
People, to give you an example, in terms of the health

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: If you are worried

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: about the Postal Service being able to deliver your bills and statements and you are worried

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_12
segments.text: about your cash flow as a large company, you are going to start thinking about alternatives. The faster we get this resolved, the faster people don't have to worry about alternatives to the mail.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: That echoes nicely with my next question. In November 2011, you addressed the National Press

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Club, and according to the transcript,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: "You know that phrase speed kills. Well, the lack of speed will kill the Postal Service. There is a stark choice,
a more

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: flexible business model that allows us to control costs quickly or very large losses that will ultimately burden the taxpayer." If immediate action is needed to return the Postal Service to solvency, why did

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: it decide to self-impose a five-month moratorium on closures and consolidations of its facilities?
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_21
segments.text: were approached by members of the Senate and they asked

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: us, in order to keep some stability with the employees and the customers, if we would agree to wait to give them an opportunity to get legislation out and over to the House and get the legislation through the House and up to the President for signature. I didn't think that was an unreasonable ask. As we worked through these processes to consolidate facilities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: It is not going to happen all at once. The way we consolidate will be done in a very thoughtful and careful method so we don't disrupt service. We are looking for the bottom line cost reductions, and we will get those, but these consolidations will happen over the course of the next year.
So

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_27
segments.text: you were supportive of the Senate's request? They

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: asked me for that consideration.
I

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_28
segments.text: had no issue with that. Chairman Ross and Chairman Iser wrote a comprehensive

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: postal reform bill last
year

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: that was passed by the subcommittee and the full oversight committee.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: It is full of cost saving measures that will revitalize the Postal Service. What parts of H.R. 2309 does the Postal Service support?
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_29
segments.text: support the FERS refund.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: We support the ability to move and consolidate the network. We support the ability to move to consolidate from six day to five day
delivery.
In your

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: written testimony,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_32
segments.text: you mentioned

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: establishing a Postal Service-sponsored health care program

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: represents the largest part of the Plan for Profitability Savings, accounting for over $7 billion of annual

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: savings.
Does

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_14
segments.text: the Postal Service have the resources to maintain its own health care plan? What
we

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_34
segments.text: would do for a health care plan is what any other company does. You go out into the free

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: market, you bid that, you find the best health care provider to act as pretty much an overall health administration firm, say a Blue Cross or a UnitedHealthcare. We would also expect to use it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: HMOs or other health care to fill the gaps because there are gaps out there and that is the way that we would manage it. We would go out through a regular competitive request for proposal and once we were able to secure the health care, the provider would manage a plan for us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_37
segments.text: And how long do you think it would take to implement such
a plan?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_09
segments.text: We have had some discussions with health care companies to understand that, to actually test out our ideas and see if they are sound. We would have to go through a request for information on RFI to get more and then go out with an actual bid. We think that we would be able to have a health care plan

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_11
segments.text: ready by 2014. Thank you,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_39
segments.text: Mr. Donahoe.
